title: lightweight-probe-sequencer-and-handoff-annotator
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds a lightweight sequential probe runner and on-call handoff annotator that improves initial triage context with compact telemetry links. Backward compatible; enabled behind feature flag 'probe_sequencer_v1'.
description:
Motivation and summary: incidents frequently start with noisy alerts and limited context in the pager handoff. This PR introduces a small, low-risk runtime component and CLI helper that sequences compact diagnostic probes (lightweight health checks, tail snippets, selected metric snapshots) for the on-call recipient and annotates the handoff message with condensed telemetry links. The goal is to reduce first-touch investigation time without adding heavy load to production systems.

What this changes (single continuous description): Implemented an in-process probe sequencer with configurable probe profiles and exponential backoff, a short-lived probe sandbox that runs non-invasive quick checks, and an annotator that attaches a 1-2 line summary + short-lived telemetry snapshot links to the incident-bot handoff payload. The feature is behind the runtime flag 'probe_sequencer_v1' and disabled by default. Added a new cli command 'incbot probe run --profile quick' for operators to run the same sequence locally during drills.

Checklist (for reviewers): 
- [x] Design doc reviewed in ENG-1148
- [x] Unit tests for sequencer scheduling and profile parsing
- [x] Integration test that simulates an alert -> handoff, verifies annotation presence and link TTL
- [x] Docs: short note in runbook README and new CLI help strings
- [x] Feature gated and env-switchable for gradual rollout

Why this approach: Prior work (ENG-937) added bulk telemetry attachments which were heavy and increased S3 usage. The sequencer approach focuses on small, targeted probes and ephemeral links to avoid storage growth while still delivering actionable context. The annotator uses existing handoff channels rather than adding a parallel notification endpoint, minimizing changes to downstream consumers.

Implementation notes: 
- probe/sequencer.go: scheduler with probe profile parsing and jittered exponential backoff; safe defaults (max 3 probes within 30s for 'quick' profile).
- probe/profiles.yaml: new default quick and extended profiles (safe, read-only diagnostics).
- handoff/annotator.go: attaches a compact summary and a telemetry link (signed URL with 1-hour TTL) to the handoff payload. Uses existing telemetry-snapshot service API.
- cli/probe_cmd.go: exposes 'incbot probe' for on-demand runs (shares sequencer engine).
- tests/*: unit tests for backoff, profile validation, and an integration test that runs a fake alert through the handler.

Commits (high-level): 
- a1b2c3d: initial sequencer scaffold and profile parsing
- b2c3d4e: implement quick profile and safe defaults; add unit tests
- c3d4e5f: annotator implementation and handoff payload wiring
- d4e5f6a: CLI command and docs; docstring and help tests
- e5f6a7b: integration test and CI flakiness fixes; address reviewer feedback

Changed areas (high level file list): 
- probe/sequencer.go
- probe/profiles.yaml
- handoff/annotator.go
- cli/probe_cmd.go
- tests/sequencer_test.go
- tests/integration/probe_handoff_test.go

Testing and CI: The initial CI run failed on a flaky timing assertion in tests/integration/probe_handoff_test.go (timeout threshold too tight). I updated the test to poll with small backoff and added a test-only tunable. Subsequent CI runs passed (unit + integration + lint). The CI summary: all checks passed on final green.

Rollout plan: Merge to main but keep feature flag off by default. Coordinate with SRE to enable for a single non-production cluster, monitor traffic and telemetry link rates for 48 hours, then expand to staging and finally prod. The CLI provides operators a way to run probes during runbook rehearsals.

Related work and notes: This is intentionally lightweight compared to the earlier telemetry blob approach; it should not materially increase object storage. Telemetry link generation uses the same signed-url service; link TTL set to 1 hour to limit retention exposure. If post-rollout metrics show excessive usage, sequencer will enforce stricter sampling and add rate limits.

Merge outcome: squash-merged after approvals and CI green.
